title: Min Stack
statement:
Design a stack that can also tell you its smallest value at any moment. It supports four operations, and each one has to run in constant time, so `getMin` can't look through the whole stack:

- `push x` puts the integer `x` on top.
- `pop` removes the top value.
- `top` returns the top value.
- `getMin` returns the smallest value in the stack.

The first line is the count `q`. Each of the next `q` lines is one operation. Print the answer to each `top` and `getMin` on its own line. The stack is never empty when a `pop`, `top`, or `getMin` comes.

Input:

```text
7
push -2
push 0
push -3
getMin
pop
top
getMin
```

Expected output:

```text
-3
0
-2
```

hints: Searching the stack on every `getMin` is too slow. Keep a second stack next to the first one.
On each push, also push the smallest value so far onto the second stack. Then its top is always the minimum, and a pop removes from both stacks.
Watch for a minimum that shows up twice. Popping one copy has to leave the other as the minimum.
